blocks.text: The hydroxyl group (-OH) is the functional group of all alcohols, which have the general formula ROH, where R is an alkyl group. The family also includes familiar substances such as cholesterol and the carbohydrates. Methanol (CH3OH) and ethanol (CH3CH2OH) are the first two members of the homologous series of monohydric alcohols.

items: By the number of -OH groups: monohydric alcohols have one (ethanol, propan-1-ol); polyhydric alcohols have more than one, e.g. ethane-1,2-diol (glycol, two) and propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol, three).

By the carbon carrying -OH: in a primary (1) alcohol, RCH2OH, it is joined to one other carbon (or none, in methanol); in a secondary (2) alcohol, R2CHOH, to two; in a tertiary (3) alcohol, R3COH, to three.

blocks.alt: Top: ethanol and propan-1-ol (monohydric), ethane-1,2-diol or glycol (dihydric) and propane-1,2,3-triol or glycerol (trihydric). Bottom: a carbon bearing OH with H, H and R (primary, RCH2OH, e.g. ethanol), with R, R and H (secondary, R2CHOH, e.g. propan-2-ol), and with three R groups (tertiary, R3COH, e.g. 2-methylpropan-2-ol).
blocks.caption: Classifying alcohols (original diagram after the book's examples).
blocks.long_description: Alcohols are sorted by how many hydroxyl groups the molecule has and, for each OH, by how many carbon atoms are bonded to the carbon carrying it. The class decides how the alcohol is oxidised.
